questions.q:
Consider the following statements about two summits in July 2026:
1. The 16th India-Japan Annual Summit, during Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's first official visit to India (1-3 July 2026), was held in Tokyo.
2. At the 3rd India-Australia Annual Summit in Melbourne on 9 July 2026, a new Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation was adopted, renewing the 2009 declaration.
3. At the same summit, the two sides finalised administrative arrangements to operationalise the 2014 civil nuclear agreement for Australian uranium supply to India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Takaichi's visit was to India, so the 16th Annual Summit took place in New Delhi, not Tokyo; statement 1 is wrong. The Melbourne summit also adopted a Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap and the Partnership on Cyber, Critical Technologies and Supply Chains (PACTS).

questions.q:
During Prime Minister Modi's visit to Jakarta on 7 July 2026, India and Indonesia signed several defence and industrial agreements. How many of the following pairs are correctly matched?
1. BrahMos missile contract : BrahMos Aerospace and Indonesia's defence ministry
2. Air-to-air missile agreement : Bharat Dynamics Ltd and Indonesia's Republikorp
3. Stainless-steel slab joint venture : SAIL and Krakatau Steel
4. Gas supply agreement : ONGC Videsh and Pertamina
questions.e: The first three agreements were signed during the visit. The ONGC Videsh-Pertamina gas supply pair is not among them. The visit was the first leg of a three-nation tour (Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand).
questions.s: The Jakarta Post and Business Today, 7 Jul 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement:
1. The Agreement was signed on 27 April 2026, and New Zealand's PM said on 9 July 2026 that 57% of New Zealand's exports to India will be tariff-free from day one.
2. New Zealand's Parliament passed legislation on 16 September 2026 to implement the Agreement.
3. The Agreement entered into force on the day it was signed in April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A trade agreement is first signed, then domestic legislation or approval is completed, and only then does it enter into force; New Zealand's law of 16 September was a step towards that, so statement 3 is wrong. The entry into force was expected around 19-20 October 2026.
questions.s: Telangana Today (PTI) and AIR News, 9 Jul and 16 Sep 2026

questions.q:
The 2026 NATO summit was held on 7-8 July 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The summit was held in Brussels, Belgium.
2. The 32 allies reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence under Article 5 of the Washington Treaty.
3. The allies pledged nearly EUR 70 billion in military assistance to Ukraine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2026 summit was hosted in Ankara, Türkiye, not at NATO's Brussels headquarters. Article 5 of the North Atlantic (Washington) Treaty treats an armed attack on one ally as an attack on all, and is the core of the alliance.

questions.q:
Andy Burnham became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned. Consider the following statements:
1. Burnham took over as Prime Minister after Starmer's resignation, without a general election being held.
2. In the UK the Prime Minister is formally appointed by the monarch, normally the person who can command the confidence of the House of Commons.
3. A change of Prime Minister in the UK requires the House of Commons to be dissolved and a general election to be held.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The UK has a parliamentary system in which the head of the majority party (or coalition) becomes Prime Minister, so a change of party leader changes the Prime Minister without any election; this has happened often (Burnham is the seventh PM in ten years). Statement 3 confuses a change of leadership with a change of government by election.

questions.q:
Bangladesh's President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on 24 July 2026 citing ill health, and Jatiya Sangsad Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed took over the president's duties until a new president is elected within 90 days. Consider the following statements:
1. The President of Bangladesh resigned on 24 July 2026 citing ill health.
2. The Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad has taken over the president's duties until a new president is elected.
3. The President of Bangladesh is elected directly by the people in a nationwide vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The President of Bangladesh is elected by members of the Jatiya Sangsad (Parliament), and the post is largely ceremonial, with executive power vested in the Prime Minister; so statement 3 is wrong. As in several parliamentary systems, the Speaker acts as President when the office falls vacant.

questions.q:
On 8 July 2026 the United States notified Congress of its intention to remove Syria from its list of State Sponsors of Terrorism. Consider the following statements:
1. The United States notified Congress on 8 July 2026 of its intention to remove Syria from the list.
2. Syria's designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism had been in place since 1979.
3. The list of State Sponsors of Terrorism is maintained by the US Department of Defense.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are as reported. The list is maintained by the US Department of State (the Secretary of State designates countries), and its removal requires notifying Congress before it takes effect, which is why a notification came first.

questions.q:
The 5th meeting of the BIMSTEC National Security Chiefs was held in New Delhi on 16 July 2026, chaired by National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, and adopted guidelines for the maritime component of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. Consider the following statements:
1. The meeting adopted guidelines for the maritime component of HADR.
2. The BIMSTEC Secretariat is located in Dhaka.
3. Pakistan and the Maldives are members of BIMSTEC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) has seven members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Pakistan and the Maldives are not members, which is one reason India has used BIMSTEC as an alternative to a stalled SAARC.
questions.s: BIMSTEC Secretariat and Business Today, 16 Jul 2026

questions.q:
President Droupadi Murmu visited Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania during 19-25 July 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. These were the first bilateral visits by an Indian President to Moldova and North Macedonia.
2. She visited Romania from 23 to 25 July 2026.
3. It was the first state visit to Romania by an Indian President since 2004.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The visit to Romania was the first state visit by an Indian President there since 1994, not 2004. The programme was Moldova on 20 July, North Macedonia on 21-22 July and Romania on 23-25 July.

questions.q:
National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held the 25th round of the India-China Special Representatives talks on the boundary question in Beijing on 25 August 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The 25th round of the Special Representatives talks was held in Beijing on 25 August 2026.
2. India's Special Representative in these talks is the National Security Adviser, while China's is its Foreign Minister.
3. The 26th round will be held in China in 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The two sides agreed that the next round, the 26th, will be held in India in 2027, alternating the venue, so statement 3 is wrong. Both sides spoke of a 'package solution' within the 2005 political parameters and welcomed the resumption of the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra and border trade through three designated passes.
questions.s: MFA PRC and Deccan Chronicle, 25 Aug 2026

questions.q:
India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) signed Terms of Reference on 12 August 2026 for negotiating a Preferential Trade Agreement, reported as India's first such ToR with an African bloc. Consider the following statements:
1. The Terms of Reference are for negotiating a Preferential Trade Agreement between India and SACU.
2. SACU's members are Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa.
3. Zimbabwe is a member of SACU.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: SACU has five members: Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa. Zimbabwe, a SADC member, is not part of this customs union. A Preferential Trade Agreement cuts tariffs on selected lines, whereas an FTA covers substantially all trade.
questions.s: IANS and SACU press release, 12 Aug 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal met Chile's Vice-Minister for International Economic Relations in Santiago on 26 August 2026 to advance the India-Chile CEPA, which India aims to conclude within 2026.
2. The India-Chile CEPA was signed on 26 August 2026.
3. India and Nepal signed MoUs on 12 August 2026 for eight High Impact Community Development Projects in education, health and agriculture, with Indian grant assistance of about NPR 803 million.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CEPA negotiations are still under way (critical minerals and market access are focus areas), so it has not been signed. The Nepal projects fall under India's grant-funded small community development projects, a standard tool of its 'Neighbourhood First' policy.

questions.q:
On 7 August 2026 the US Senate passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by 86-11. Consider the following statements:
1. The Senate passed the Bill by 86 votes to 11 on 7 August 2026.
2. It would let the US President impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries among the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas.
3. India is among the countries named as top five buyers of Russian oil and gas.
4. The tariffs would apply automatically to all named countries without any Presidential discretion.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Bill names China, India, Azerbaijan, Hungary and Slovakia, but only 'lets' the President impose tariffs; it is not automatic, and the Bill still needed House approval before it could go to the President. Statement 4 ignores the discretion.

questions.q: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar visited Russia on 23-24 August 2026 and met President Vladimir Putin on 24 August. The visit took place ahead of Putin's expected visit to New Delhi to attend the
questions.e: India is the 2026 BRICS chair and hosted the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 12-13 September 2026. The SCO summit of 2026 was in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, and not in New Delhi.
questions.s: Bridge Chronicle and Telangana Today, 24 Aug 2026

questions.q:
On 27 August 2026 India announced that the 18th BRICS Summit would be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 12-13 September 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The summit's theme is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.
2. India holds the BRICS chairship in 2026 for the fourth time.
3. The BRICS Heads of Anti-Drug Agencies meeting in Guwahati on 6-7 July 2026 under India's chairship adopted the Guwahati Declaration.
4. India had earlier chaired BRICS in 2012, 2016 and 2019.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's earlier BRICS chairships were in 2012, 2016 and 2021, so statement 4 is wrong (2019 was Brazil's year). 2026 is therefore India's fourth turn and also BRICS's 20th year.
questions.s: AIR and PIB/NCB, 27 Aug and 7 Jul 2026

questions.q:
During Prime Minister Modi's state visit to Uzbekistan in late August 2026, India and Uzbekistan upgraded their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Consider the following statements:
1. The relationship was upgraded to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
2. The two sides agreed on a framework for long-term supply of uranium to India.
3. Uzbekistan is not a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Uzbekistan is a founding member of the SCO (it joined in 2001, the year the grouping was formed from the Shanghai Five), so statement 3 is wrong. Uranium supply is part of India's push to diversify nuclear fuel sources after the SHANTI Act opened the nuclear sector.
questions.s: All India Radio and ThePrint, 30 Aug 2026

questions.q:
The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit was held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan on 1 September 2026, and Prime Minister Modi attended. Consider the following statements:
1. The Summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration.
2. The Summit marked the 25th anniversary of the SCO, which was founded in 2001.
3. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2005.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India (with Pakistan) became a full SCO member in 2017; in 2005 it joined only as an observer. The grouping began in 2001 with six members, and the Bishkek summit marked its silver jubilee.

questions.q:
On 4 September 2026 the UN General Assembly adopted the 'Correct the Map' resolution promoting equal-area world maps by 164 votes in favour to 1 against, with 6 abstentions. Consider the following statements:
1. The resolution was adopted by 164 votes to 1, with 6 abstentions.
2. The resolution is non-binding.
3. India voted against the resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India voted in favour but reserved its position on political boundaries, with the MEA stressing that maps must show J&K and Ladakh as in India's official map. General Assembly resolutions are recommendatory, not legally binding. The African-led initiative targets the Mercator projection, which exaggerates the size of high-latitude regions.
questions.s: The Print and Outlook India, 4 Sep 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On 24 September 2026 the UN General Assembly adopted by consensus its first Declaration on Sea Level Rise.
2. The Declaration states that States threatened by rising seas do not automatically lose statehood and may retain their UNCLOS maritime zones.
3. India was among the initial co-sponsors of the Partners for Multilateralism declaration adopted at its inaugural summit at the UN on 21 September 2026.
4. A General Assembly declaration of this kind creates legally binding obligations on all UN member States.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Declaration affirms that low-lying island States keep their statehood and maritime entitlements under UNCLOS even if the coastline shifts, which matters for Pacific island nations. General Assembly declarations are politically and legally influential but not binding on States, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Down To Earth and Adda247, 21-24 Sep 2026

questions.q:
On 22 September 2026 the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed a security agreement expanding US military access to Greenland. Consider the following statements:
1. The agreement expands US military access to Greenland.
2. It leaves Greenland's territorial status unchanged.
3. Greenland is a sovereign State and a full member of the United Nations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Greenland is an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark, which still speaks for it in foreign and defence affairs, and it is not a UN member. That is why Denmark is a party to the agreement, which followed repeated US demands to acquire Greenland.

questions.q:
On 16 September 2026 the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of war crimes and sentenced him to 25 years' imprisonment. Consider the following statements:
1. The Chambers convicted and sentenced Thaci to 25 years' imprisonment.
2. The Kosovo Specialist Chambers are a part of the International Criminal Court.
3. Thaci is a former President of Kosovo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Chambers are an EU-backed court, based in The Hague, set up to try crimes of the 1998-99 Kosovo conflict; they are not part of the ICC, which is the permanent court under the Rome Statute. The ICC (statute-based) and ICJ (State disputes) are different bodies.

questions.q:
On 14 September 2026 India and MERCOSUR signed the First Additional Protocol to their Preferential Trade Agreement recognising electronic Certificates of Origin. Consider the following statements:
1. The Protocol recognises electronic Certificates of Origin, and the two sides announced talks to expand the PTA.
2. MERCOSUR comprises Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay (Bolivia has acceded).
3. Chile is a full member of MERCOSUR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MERCOSUR's core members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, with Bolivia having acceded; Chile is only an associate State, which is why India negotiates a separate CEPA with Chile. A certificate of origin proves where goods were made, so that they qualify for preferential tariffs.

questions.q:
The 19th India-Vietnam Joint Commission Meeting was co-chaired by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung on 14 September 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The meeting was held in New Delhi and reviewed the Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
2. The two sides agreed to observe a Friendship Year in 2027.
3. The meeting was held in Hanoi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The meeting was co-chaired in New Delhi, so statement 3 is wrong (Joint Commission meetings alternate between the two capitals). Defence co-production, market access and connectivity were flagged as areas for deeper cooperation.

questions.q:
India welcomed the Philippines' decision to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) during Prime Minister Modi's meeting with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in New Delhi on 13 September 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The Philippines decided to join CDRI, which India welcomed during the bilateral meeting of 13 September 2026.
2. CDRI is an India-led global partnership launched in 2019 at the UN Climate Action Summit.
3. CDRI's secretariat is located in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CDRI is an India-led global partnership whose secretariat is in New Delhi, not Geneva. It promotes disaster-resilient infrastructure, like the earlier India-led International Solar Alliance.
questions.s: Philippine Daily Tribune and The Star, 13 Sep 2026

questions.q:
The FATF report 'Investigating Professional Money Laundering, Underground Banking, and the Use of Hawala and Other Similar Service Providers' (September 2026) found that virtual assets are fusing with traditional hawala networks. Consider the following statements:
1. The report found that virtual assets are fusing with traditional hawala networks.
2. The Financial Action Task Force is an inter-governmental body headquartered in Paris.
3. India became a member of the FATF in 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India joined the FATF in 2010, not 2000. The FATF sets global standards against money laundering and terror financing, and hawala is an informal value-transfer system, now increasingly combined with crypto channels.
